source.title: Intrinsic Structure: Spectral Identifiability for Mechanistic Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different representation and intervention from the original circuit analysis: it ablates Koopman modes and other directions, then measures IOI logit effects. This bears on the IOI evaluation and partial-behaviour aspect of V5, but does not intervene on the claimed 26-head circuit.
record.gate_note: The IOI results compare ablations of Koopman modes, PCA directions, and random directions on GPT-2 small. The paper also measures modal alignment with known IOI head classes and reproducibility of selected modes; these do not establish whether the claimed heads themselves play their stated roles under patching or whether the claimed circuit is faithful, complete, or minimal. The held-out read-out reconstruction error is a precondition for the analysis, not an IOI circuit result.
record.test_reason: The study uses the IOI task and the known head classes of the original paper as a testbed for its own Koopman-mode method. In GPT-2 small at layer 9 it ablates Koopman modes, PCA directions and random directions and reports how much IOI logit difference each removes. It also measures how well the modal basis aligns with known head subspaces. None of this intervenes on the 26-head circuit or evaluates its faithfulness, completeness or minimality under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions. It does not test backups, other models' IOI circuits, other circuit-finding methods, or prompt variants. The results show how good the Koopman method is, not whether any version holds. The reader's V5 link conflates 'direction-set ablations remove part of the logit difference' with 'the circuit explains only part of the behaviour'.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that Koopman modes carry behaviourally relevant structure but do not resolve the IOI circuit. The modes beat random directions but lose to PCA, and they align only weakly with known head subspaces. The selected mode set is not reproducible across calibration draws. The authors attribute the gap to non-normality, as their dissociation theorem predicts. The spectrum is an identifiable model fingerprint, not a human-legible decomposition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Koopman spectral representation and rank-j direction ablations with IOI logit difference as the measure; does not reproduce the original head ablations, patching, or faithfulness/completeness/minimality evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: For GPT-2 small at layer 9, the reported IOI ablation effect differs by direction set (Koopman modes, PCA, random) and by j. The IOI analysis uses 4,096 prompts balanced across 15 templates; prompt distribution is not varied.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 small at layer 9, ablating the top-j Koopman modes removes 25% (j=8) and 41% (j=32) of the IOI logit difference. PCA directions remove 60% and 67%, and random directions never exceed 7%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-rank residual-stream directions such as principal components carry a large share of the IOI logit difference at layer 9; Koopman modes carry less.

fits_no_version.finding: The Koopman modal basis aligns only modestly with known IOI head subspaces: 0.260 for name movers, 0.311 for S-inhibition and 0.298 for induction heads, against a null of 0.125. The top-16 selected mode subspace agrees only 0.290 across calibration draws.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Koopman spectral modes do not reproducibly recover the IOI head classes in GPT-2 small.

record.problems: The IOI evaluation is limited to GPT-2 small at layer 9 and one prompt collection. The study does not intervene on the claimed circuit's heads, test backup-head self-repair, or evaluate the circuit's stated faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. Uncertainty for the reported IOI ablation percentages and alignment values is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No reported IOI ablation or head-alignment results were left out. The held-out read-out reconstruction error is described as a precondition for the analysis and is not a direct IOI circuit finding, so it was not recorded as a row.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit, its head roles under patching, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
Ablation of the name-mover heads and takeover by backup heads.
IOI circuits in other models, sizes or checkpoints, and reuse of components for other tasks. The other models are used only for spectral analyses.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics recover the same circuit.

Dependence of the circuit's faithfulness and completeness on ablation type, metric or prompt distribution, and the fraction of the behaviour the circuit explains. Only one prompt set is used, and no ablation is applied to the circuit.
The circuit across name orders, templates or more names. The 15 templates are pooled.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 and the V5 limits_scope label are dropped: IOI is a testbed for evaluating Koopman modes, so the study is T4. Section 11.4 has further projection ablations (27% vs 34% at j=32 with forward projection). These are also method results and bear on no version. The IOI circuit is taken as ground truth, not tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the claimed 26-head, 7-class circuit, or its faithfulness, completeness, minimality, or head roles under patching.
Does not ablate main name-mover heads or test backup-head self-repair.
Although the study includes other models for its spectral analyses, it does not test whether the IOI circuit or its head classes and roles recur in them, checkpoints, or other tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics for recovery of the claimed circuit.

Tests IOI logit effects for alternative direction sets at one layer and one prompt collection, not the sensitivity or completeness of the claimed head circuit itself; it does not vary prompt distribution or evaluate the circuit under multiple metrics.
Does not test the claimed circuit across name orders, templates, or numbers of names as separate conditions.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 small, layer 9, 4,096 prompts across 15 templates; mode and PCA direction ablations at j=8 and j=32
reader_labels.reason: The tested direction ablations remove only part of the IOI logit difference, and the measured effect differs substantially by direction set: Koopman modes remove less than PCA directions (r1, r2, r4, r5). Random directions have a still smaller effect (r3). This does not establish the completeness of the claimed head circuit.
